verdict.summary: Creating a Manage app and connecting your own account is quick, but first you need a Clio Manage account: a 7-day trial in each region, then a developer account Clio has to approve. Clio's docs also say creating an app needs a paid account. Getting listed in the App Directory means passing Clio's Application Security and Compliance review, sending a recorded demo and going through listing review. Clio publishes no timeline for any of this.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for the app and a test connection; several days to prepare policies, the security questionnaire, the demo and the listing
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 30-60 min after you have a Clio Manage trial or paid account
verdict.approval_wait: Unknown. Clio publishes no timeline for the developer-account application, the security review or the App Directory listing.

gates.name: Developer Application on your own trial/developer account
gates.unlocks: You can create the Developer Application, get the App Key and App Secret, and authorize your own Clio Manage account.
limits: No sandbox: you test against your own Manage trial or developer account
The trial lasts 7 days, then you have to apply for a free developer account
Clio's private-app page says creating an app needs access to a paid Clio account. The EasyStart tier cannot use apps.
You need a separate account, with a different email, for each region (US/EU/CA/AU)
Access tokens expire after 30 days. Refresh tokens do not expire.
Rate limit: 50 requests per minute per access token at peak hours
gates.time_to_reach: About 30 minutes once you have a Manage account. The trial starts right away. Converting it to a developer account waits on Clio's review.

gates.name: Private app (unreviewed)
gates.unlocks: The same app can be used with other Clio Manage accounts you have login credentials for, such as your own firm or a client firm that runs its own integration. Clio does not review private apps.
limits: Cannot be listed in the Clio App Directory
Clio documents no install caps or test-user allowlist
Tokens are region-specific: US tokens do not work against EU, CA or AU endpoints
Clio can block Public API access for an app if it sees security red flags

gates.name: Public app / App Directory listing
gates.unlocks: A public app that any Clio Manage firm can find and install from the Clio App Directory.
limits: Must pass the Application Security and Compliance review
Must provide onboarding content specific to the integration, support the latest two versions of major browsers, and keep at least 99% uptime over a rolling 30 days
Must publish terms of service, a privacy policy and a security policy, and serve the app over HTTPS
gates.time_to_reach: Not published by Clio. Plan on weeks: questionnaire, security review, demo, listing form and draft review.

steps.title: Start a Clio Manage trial in each region you need
steps.detail: Sign up for a free 7-day Clio Manage trial. It is your test environment because Clio has no sandbox, and its Manage login also signs you in to the developer portal. If you will serve several regions (US, EU, CA, AU), create one trial per region, each with a different email address.
gotchas: Apps and integrations are not available on the EasyStart tier

steps.title: Apply to convert the trial into a free developer account
steps.detail: Before the 7-day trial runs out, submit Clio's developer-account intake form. Clio reviews the application and, if you are eligible, converts the trial into a developer account.
steps.est_time: 15 min plus Clio review time (not published)
gotchas: Clio's private-app page says creating an app requires access to a paid Clio account. If app creation is blocked on your trial, use a paid firm account or wait for the developer account.

steps.title: Open the Manage developer portal and create a new app
steps.detail: Go to developers.clio.com and sign in with your Clio Manage credentials. Then open the new-app form at developers.clio.com/apps/new. Your apps appear under Developer Apps.
gotchas: This is the Manage portal. Clio Platform (Grow) uses a separate portal and needs a separate app.

steps.title: Fill in the app details and redirect URI
steps.detail: Enter Name and Website URL, add the Redirect URI, and accept the Developer Terms of Service. Users see the name, description, icon and website on the OAuth approval screen, so use your real product details. Description, Icons and Support URL are optional.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The redirect_uri in the authorize and token requests must exactly match a saved Redirect URI

steps.title: Select the minimum App Permissions
steps.detail: Map each API call your agent makes to a Manage permission (for example Matters, Contacts, Tasks, Calendar, Documents) and choose Read or Read/Write for each. Request the smallest set that works. Some endpoints need two permissions: Matter Clients and Relationships need both Matters and Contacts. Webhooks need the scope for each model you subscribe to plus the webhooks scope.
gotchas: If you add permissions later, existing users keep their old grants until they reauthorize

steps.title: Copy the App Key and App Secret into your Composio auth config
steps.detail: After you save, the portal shows an App Key (the client_id) and an App Secret (the client_secret). Composio has no Clio toolkit, so set up a custom OAuth2 auth config with these credentials and the app.clio.com authorize and token endpoints (or your region's host). Note the App ID from the portal's app table, because Clio support asks for it.
gotchas: The App ID is not the same as the App Key, and App IDs differ by region
Keep the secret in environment variables or a secrets store, never in client code

steps.title: Run a test authorization against your own account
steps.detail: Start the flow with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri and a state value, then approve it in your Manage account. The code must be exchanged within 10 minutes by a form-encoded POST to the token endpoint. Confirm you get back a bearer access_token, a refresh_token and expires_in (2592000 seconds, i.e. 30 days). Optionally add redirect_on_decline=true so a declined grant returns error=access_denied instead of a Clio 400 page.
gotchas: Tokens from app.clio.com do not work against EU, CA or AU base URLs
A 403 can come from the user's Manage role rather than a missing scope

steps.title: Handle token refresh and set a deauthorization callback
steps.detail: When a call returns 401, refresh with grant_type=refresh_token. Manage refresh tokens do not expire and can be reused, so store them encrypted. Optionally set a Deauthorization Callback URL so your app gets a JSON POST (client_id, user_id, token or 'all') whenever a user revokes access.

steps.title: Publish your terms of service, privacy policy and security policy
steps.detail: Draft and publish terms of service, a privacy policy and a security policy, and serve everything over HTTPS. Clio requires these, and the review will look for them. List any SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS or TRUSTe certifications you hold, because Clio says they make approval faster.

steps.title: Request and complete the security and compliance questionnaire
steps.detail: Email Clio's API Partnerships team to ask for the Application Security and Compliance questionnaire, then complete and return it. An agent can draft the answers from your security documentation.

steps.title: Wait for the security review
steps.detail: API Partnerships either approves the integration or asks for changes. If you fail, Clio sends feedback and works with you until the app meets the standard.
gotchas: Red flags can lead Clio to decline the listing and/or block the app's Public API access

steps.title: Send a pre-recorded demo to API Partnerships
steps.detail: Once the security review is approved, record a demo of the integration and email it to API Partnerships.

steps.title: Submit the App Directory listing and approve the draft
steps.detail: Complete the App Directory listing form, including onboarding content specific to your integration. Review the draft listing page Clio sends you, after which the API Partnerships team launches it publicly.

requirements.item: Clio Manage trial or developer account in each target region, each with its own email
requirements.detail: There is no sandbox. You test against your own Manage account, and each region needs a separate account.

requirements.item: Access to a paid Clio account (not EasyStart) to create an app
requirements.detail: Clio's private-app page states this requirement. Check whether your trial or developer account meets it.

requirements.item: App Name, Website URL, Redirect URI(s), accepted Developer ToS, App Permissions
requirements.detail: These fields are required on the Manage app creation form.

requirements.item: HTTPS, secret kept private, published ToS, privacy policy and security policy
requirements.detail: These come from Clio's developer security and data guidelines.

requirements.item: Passed Application Security and Compliance review
requirements.detail: You request the questionnaire from API Partnerships by email.

requirements.item: Onboarding content, support for the latest two browser versions, at least 99% uptime over a rolling 30 days
requirements.detail: These are the App Directory requirements in Clio's App Developer Guide.

requirements.item: Pre-recorded demo and App Directory listing form
requirements.detail: You send these after security approval and before public launch.

scopes.scope: Resource permissions (e.g. Matters, Contacts, Tasks, Calendar, Documents, Bills, Users), Read
scopes.effect: Allows GET on the resource and related endpoints. Chosen on the app form. Clio documents no extra review per scope.
Adds create, update and delete. Request write only where your agent needs it. Clio documents no separate review for write permissions.
Both are required for the Matter Clients and Relationships endpoints.
A separate webhooks scope, needed in addition to the scope for each subscribed model.

blockers.symptom: Cannot create an app or get an App Key/Secret
blockers.cause: Clio says creating an app requires access to a paid Clio account. EasyStart accounts cannot use apps, and trials expire after 7 days.
blockers.fix: Apply for the free developer account before the trial ends, or use a paid (non-EasyStart) firm account.

blockers.symptom: Users see 401 errors or invalid tokens in the EU, Canada or Australia
blockers.cause: Tokens are region-specific. Tokens issued on app.clio.com (US) do not work against EU, CA or AU hosts, and App IDs differ by region.
blockers.fix: Create the app and accounts in each region and route each user to the base URL for their region.

blockers.cause: Either the app lacks the permission, or the user's Manage role does not allow the action.
blockers.fix: Add the permission and have the user reauthorize. If the role is the cause, the firm administrator has to change the user's role.

blockers.symptom: Security review fails, App Directory listing is declined, or Public API access is blocked
blockers.cause: Clio found security red flags or missing policies.
blockers.fix: Fix the issues in Clio's feedback, publish ToS, privacy and security policies, use HTTPS, and include any certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001) you hold.

blockers.symptom: Code exchange fails with redirect mismatch or an expired code
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri does not exactly match the saved value, or more than 10 minutes passed before the exchange.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL into the app's Redirect URIs and exchange the code right away.

composio.note: Composio's catalog has no Clio toolkit, so there is no managed app to start on. You need to register your own Clio Manage Developer Application and enter its App Key (client_id) and App Secret in a custom OAuth2 auth config. Clio documents the endpoints as https://app.clio.com/oauth/authorize and https://app.clio.com/oauth/token, and EU, CA and AU use their own hosts. Check the Composio dashboard to confirm custom Clio auth is supported before relying on it.

evidence.claim: The Clio Manage developer portal at developers.clio.com redirects to a Clio sign-in page.
The Manage developer portal uses Manage accounts for sign-in, and Manage developer signup starts with a trial.
Developers start with a free 7-day trial per region, and the trial is the test environment because there is no sandbox.
After the trial, developers apply through an intake form, and Clio reviews and converts eligible trials into developer accounts.
Multi-region apps need a separate account per region, each with a different email.
Creating a Manage app requires access to a paid Clio account, and apps are not available on EasyStart.
Private Manage apps are not reviewed, cannot be listed in the App Directory, and need credentials for the account that uses them.
Apps are created at developers.clio.com/apps/new and then show an App Key and App Secret.
Required fields are Name, Website URL, Redirect URIs, Developer ToS acceptance and App Permissions.
Name, description, icon and website appear on the OAuth approval screen.
The App ID differs from the App Key and differs by region, and support asks for it.
The authorize request needs client_id, response_type=code and a redirect_uri matching a saved value, and state is recommended.
The code is valid for 10 minutes, and the exchange is a form-encoded POST to app.clio.com/oauth/token.
The token response includes a bearer access_token, a refresh_token and expires_in of 2592000.
Access tokens expire after 30 days and are refreshed with grant_type refresh_token.
Refresh tokens do not expire, can be reused, and should be stored encrypted.
redirect_on_decline=true returns error=access_denied to the redirect URI.
The deauthorization callback receives a JSON POST when a token is revoked.
The Manage docs do not describe PKCE; only the Platform app form has a PKCE option.
Permissions are selected at app creation, and developers should request the minimum.
Each permission can be read-only or read/write.
Matter Clients and Relationships need both the Matters and Contacts permissions.
Changed permissions need users to reauthorize.
A 403 can come from a missing scope or from the user's Manage role.
Webhooks need the model scopes plus a webhooks scope.
The Manage and Platform APIs need separate apps and separate authorizations.
The rate limit is 50 requests per minute per token at peak hours, with a 429 and Retry-After when exceeded.
Security guidelines require HTTPS, a private key and secret, and published ToS, security and privacy policies.
Red flags can lead Clio to decline a listing or block Public API access, and certifications streamline approval.
Public listing goes through a security and compliance review, with the questionnaire requested from API Partnerships.
After security approval come a demo, a listing form, a draft listing review and public launch.
Directory requirements are a security review, onboarding content, support for two browser versions and 99% uptime.
Public Clio apps must go through Clio's approval process and follow the security guidelines.
After a failed security review, Clio gives feedback and works with the developer.
Testing happens only against your own trial or developer account, with no sandbox.
US tokens are not valid against EU, CA or AU endpoints.
The portal lists apps under Developer Apps, and sign-in needs no separate developer signup.

open_questions: Clio publishes no timeline for the developer-account application, the security review, the demo or the App Directory listing.
It is unclear whether a free trial or developer account meets the 'paid Clio account' requirement for creating apps.
It is unclear whether an unreviewed, unlisted Manage app can be authorized by arbitrary Clio firms. Clio documents no install caps, but it says public apps must go through approval.
Whether Manage apps support PKCE is not confirmed.
The full list of Manage permission names shown in the portal was not enumerated.
Composio has no Clio toolkit, and whether a custom OAuth2 auth config works with Clio Manage was not verified.
Some Clio support articles (such as the App Developer Guide) are old and may not reflect the current process.
